A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 26 pages, including appendices A–F, are available and readable; text and rendered-page comparisons establish localized differences.

before.justification: v4 reports original membership-inference experiments on DDIM, Stable Diffusion and DiT, including attack-performance measurements and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary analyses, with revised reporting in Table 15.

M1.justification: The attack formalization and proposed Fourier-domain filtering procedure, including Equations 9–11, are unchanged. Relabeling the attack used in an ablation does not revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.7 and Table 15 change the reported dataset for the DDIM parameter sweep from Tiny-IN to CIFAR-100. Both already appear in Table 2, so this is a limited revision to reported ablation coverage, without an expanded benchmark suite.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain the same baseline methods, including Naive, SecMI, PIA and CLID. Table 15 relabels the attack underlying a filter-parameter sweep from Naive to PIA; it does not add or remove an independently evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Table 15 changes the sweep’s reported attack configuration from Naive to PIA, alongside its dataset reassignment. The parameter grid and ASR/AUC metrics remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing DDIM sensitivity analysis in Appendix D.7 is reassigned to PIA/CIFAR-100 and its default-setting result is corrected. The sensitivity question, parameter recommendations and other ablation, robustness and supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The normality tests and statistical reporting in Appendix D.2 are unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: At r_t=5 and s=0.2, Table 15 changes ASR from 85.03 to 85.05 and AUC from 92.22 to 92.20. Its attack/dataset attribution also changes, preventing a same-setting performance comparison. Other numerical results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Proposition 4.2 and derivations and proofs in Appendices B–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about high-frequency deficiency, the general attack paradigm and the effectiveness of the proposed filter.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of hyperparameter robustness and limitations concerning pretrained models and the Gaussian approximation are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and resource disclosures in Section 5.1, Appendix D.3, Appendix D.8 and Appendix F are unchanged, including hardware, training settings, runtime and code/data access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, bibliography and positioning relative to prior research are unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds a funding acknowledgment, updates the arXiv version/date stamp and revises the dataset and attack wording in Appendix D.7 and Table 15. The remaining narrative and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 15’s caption changes, and the expanded acknowledgment causes local text reflow on page 9. Figures and table structures remain unchanged, including Figure 7’s Naive/Tiny-IN panel labels.

improvement.justification: The revised PIA/CIFAR-100 attribution and default values in Table 15 now agree with the existing PIA+F/CIFAR-100 result in Table 2, improving internal consistency. The benefit is limited: the scientific contribution is unchanged, and Figure 7 retains Naive/Tiny-IN labels, leaving its relationship to the revised ablation table unclear.
